title: Idempotency Keys Under Distributed Retry Pressure: Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Chronos-Interpreter

author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: Distributed payment services must guarantee that repeated client requests do not trigger duplicate side effects. We present a deterministic key-scoping mechanism that derives a unique identifier from tenant, operation, and payload hash, and a bounded LRU store that guarantees $O(1)$ amortised lookup, insertion, and eviction while preserving a strict height-balanced invariant. The implementation is in Chronos-Interpreter and achieves a mean latency of 182 310 \textmu{}s with a throughput of 5 485 ops/s on an AMD EPYC 7763 host. The design is formally verified to maintain the key-ordered invariant and to bound the store size by the configured capacity.
